note:
Header banner for /pages/acetyl-hexapeptide-8-research, and the fix for a page that was BROKEN rather than merely off-brand.

THE FAULT. The hero pointed at skingenetix-research-acetyl-hexapeptide-8-banner.jpg, which 404s on the CDN - the file does not exist in Files. The section therefore fell back to Shopify's own placeholder artwork, so a live research page was showing line drawings of a handbag, a shoe and a feather behind its heading. It also explains the 3KB reading for this page in the banner audit, where every working banner measures 20-63KB.

AUDITED AGAINST THE PAGES THAT WORK before changing anything. Structure was never the problem: this template carries the same eight sections in the same order as research-matrixyl and research-copper-peptide, with the same block counts - overview 3, key findings 3, FAQ 5, related 4 - and comparable content weight throughout. Only the hero was wrong, in exactly two ways: the missing image, and overlay_opacity at 50 where the working research pages sit at 22-25. Fifty is the stale theme default this project has already recorded as muting a picture to near-flat.

THE IMAGE. AHR-3-SIGNAL-DAMPED nbp_pro_01, from a six-concept batch. Chosen because it is the only concept that IS the mechanism rather than decoration around it: Acetyl Hexapeptide-8 damps the neurotransmitter signalling that drives repeated micro-contraction, and the picture is a wave losing amplitude from left to right until it lies flat. Measured centre block 19.9 mean / 10.9 stdev before cropping, 20.3 / 12.7 after - dark and even under a centred white heading.

CROPPED, NOT EXTENDED. The band is 100vw x 496px, needing about 3.9:1 to hold full height at 1920; the source is 2.357:1. 531px came off the top and bottom symmetrically - symmetric because the wave sits on the vertical centre line, unlike the matrixyl banner whose bright fibres were all at the top and needed a one-sided crop. No invented pixels.

A MOBILE IMAGE IS SET, which research-matrixyl still lacks. research-copper-peptide is the only research page that had one, and it is the right pattern: a 3.9:1 band centre-cropped on a phone keeps almost nothing. The phone crop keeps the left of the frame, where the wave still has amplitude.

RATIO CORRECTED AFTER MEASURING THE LIVE BAND. The first crop used 3.9:1, carried over from the matrixyl research page. That was wrong for THIS page: measured live, its band is 100vw x 440px, not the matrixyl page's 496px, because its heading is one line rather than four - the band's height follows its content. At 3.899:1 the image held full height at 1440 but only 89% at 1920. Rebuilt at 4.400:1, which clears the 4.364:1 the band reaches at 1920. The lesson is that the target aspect is a property of the PAGE, not of the theme: two pages using the same section type differ by 56px of band height purely because one heading wraps.

SILK REPLACES THE WAVE. Malcolm rejected the damping-wave banner and asked for silver silk. The first silk attempt had already lost a batch on measurement - its four candidates scored centre-block means of 45, 54, 58 and 65 against a best of 14 - because every engine filled the frame with fabric, and lit silk is bright by definition. The re-brief made the dark area a matter of GEOMETRY rather than of lighting mood: each concept states which part of the frame the silk occupies and declares the rest genuinely empty. That worked - the new batch's best centre measured 2.2.

THE HEADING MOVES RIGHT, AND THAT IS THE REAL FIX HERE. The chosen frame puts the silk on the LEFT and falls to empty graphite on the right. Measured across the width where the heading sits: 176 mean at the far left, 87, then 48, then 28 with a stdev of 1.4 across the right third. A centred heading would straddle lit fabric at mean 43.6 / stdev 21.7; moved to centre-end it sits at 29.0 / stdev 2.2. One setting, and it is established on these pages already - research-copper-peptide runs an off-centre heading too.

The phone crop is taken from 30% across rather than from the edge, so it keeps the silk fold at its left and dark ground to the right, instead of being either a wall of fabric or an empty rectangle.
